content:
Quick answer: Fatigue in arthritis can reflect inflammation, pain, poor sleep, mood, medication effects or other conditions. Persistent or worsening fatigue deserves assessment rather than being assumed to be caused by arthritis alone.

Why fatigue happens

Inflammatory disease, disrupted sleep, pain and stress can contribute. Anaemia, thyroid disorders, infection and other causes may also need consideration by a clinician.

Pacing and activity

Break demanding tasks into manageable parts, alternate activity with rest and keep a simple symptom diary. Gentle regular activity may support function, but avoid pushing through severe exhaustion.

Sleep and support

Keep a consistent sleep routine where possible and discuss pain control or sleep problems with your care team. Ask for support with work and daily tasks if fatigue affects safety.

When to seek medical advice

Contact your GP for persistent new fatigue, unexplained weight loss, fever, breathlessness or significant deterioration. Seek emergency help for severe chest pain, collapse or severe breathlessness.
